title: Generate run-local LDBC queryDir compatibility files and broaden native smoke coverage

steps.step: Continue from BENCHPROD-111 missing PostgreSQL query/update SQL file gaps
Generate a run-local ldbc_queries directory instead of modifying the external ldbc-snb checkout
Add compatibility aliases and inline update SQL files required by the PostgreSQL implementation loader
Run Q14-enabled 10-op native command-mode smoke to confirm query-load stderr is gone
Broaden to an 80-op command-mode smoke and classify newly exposed LDBC blockers
Fix timestamp/date/interval arithmetic needed by the LdbcQuery4 SQL shape
Fix ORDER BY projection preference for the LdbcQuery7 ambiguous l_creationdate shape
Run focused isolation checks for Q6, Q7, Q12, and Q13
Rerun the broadened 80-op command-mode smoke after the interval and ORDER BY fixes
Record evidence conservatively as native command-mode smoke, not a full official LDBC pass

result.smoke_scope: command-mode LDBC SNB Interactive PostgreSQL implementation, preloaded PostgreSQL test-data, run-local compatibility queryDir, updates disabled, Q14 indexes enabled, 80 requested operations, warmup 0, duration 20 seconds

isolation_findings.LdbcQuery6: ldbc_command timed out after 180 seconds with 2 of 3 operations completed; treat as performance blocker, not a confirmed functional error.
isolation_findings.LdbcQuery7: ldbc_command passed after ORDER BY projection preference fix; isolation summary remains gap by design because isolation mode disables other read queries.
isolation_findings.LdbcQuery12: ldbc_command passed, 1 operation at 181 ms; isolation summary remains gap by design.
isolation_findings.LdbcQuery13: ldbc_command passed, 1 operation at 93 ms; isolation summary remains gap by design.

result.stderr_boundary: Final broad smoke no longer reports Unable to load query; stderr contains only SLF4J no-provider warnings.

remaining_blockers: This is not a full official/native LDBC benchmark pass.
Updates remain disabled in the generated LDBC properties even though compatibility update SQL files are now present.
The final broad 80-op stream did not exercise every complex query in one run; Q7, Q12, and Q13 are covered only by isolation commands.
LdbcQuery6 remains a performance blocker and timed out in isolation after 180 seconds.
LdbcQuery4 is functionally passing but very slow at about 41.3 seconds for one operation.
Native memtier remains blocked by missing real memtier_benchmark tooling.
next_task: BENCHPROD-113 candidate: optimize LdbcQuery6 performance, starting from the isolate_q6 timeout evidence and Q6 SQL shape.
